title: Do three kinds of self-replicating spots with cyclic predation on one regrowing feed coexist in spirals only in domains large enough for the spirals, as rock-paper-scissors theory predicts?
summary: Reichenbach, Mobilia & Frey (Nature 448, 1046, 2007) show that cyclic (rock-paper-scissors) competition gives coexistence in entangled spirals only below a critical mobility, M_c = (4.5 ± 0.5)e-4 in the lattice model, and that biodiversity is lost once the spiral wavelength outgrows the system. Neither the ledger nor LITERATURE.md has a cyclic-dominance or predator-prey ecology of reproducing bodies. Here three Gray-Scott spot kinds share one feed and prey on each other in a cycle, against transitive and no-predation twins. A coexistence threshold in domain size would be a falsifiable law for C:ecology-with-reproduction.

sources.cite: Reichenbach, Mobilia & Frey, Mobility promotes and jeopardizes biodiversity in rock-paper-scissors games, Nature 448, 1046-1049 (2007), arXiv:0709.0217. The synthesizer re-opened the PDF and confirmed M_c = (4.5 ± 0.5)e-4 and that wavelength scales with mobility up to a universal lambda_c.
